ddx.step1_summary:
- Chief complaint: Soreness and cracking dry skin of the hands, predominantly the palms, present for about 3–4 months and now painful enough to affect work.
- Symptoms: Severe dryness with fissures/cracks on palms; itching (not constant but present); occasional bleeding when scratched; no fever, nausea, vomiting, bowel or urinary symptoms; general appetite and wellbeing maintained.
- Onset/ course: Symptoms started a few months ago, gradually worsening; currently limiting ability to work as a hotel housekeeper.
- Distribution: Palms mainly; dryness noted on legs as milder, non-severe.
- Aggravating/ alleviating factors: Likely exposure to cleaning products at work with intermittent glove use (recent job change ~4 months ago); symptoms worse with use of cleaning chemicals; tried OTC moisturizers (E45) and antihistamines without relief.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (on metformin).
- Medications/allergies: Metformin; no known allergies.
- Family/social history: Works as a housekeeper for a hotel; sometimes does not wear gloves while cleaning; no smoking; drinks a couple pints of alcohol per week; family history notable for diabetes.
- Vital signs/exam findings (transcript-based): Exam describes palms that are very cracked, dry, and itchy with occasional scratching-induced bleeding; no systemic symptoms reported.
- Labs/imaging: none mentioned.
- Plan discussed: Advise use of gloves during cleaning; start topical corticosteroid for inflammation; use stronger emollients (moisturizers) several times daily for 2 weeks; follow-up in 1–2 weeks or sooner if worse or spreading; prescription to be sent to pharmacy.

I: Irritant contact dermatitis: Likely given occupational exposure to cleaning products and inconsistent glove use, palm-predominant involvement, itching, and cracking. Correlation with job duties (hotel cleaning) and recent change in work role supports this.

Allergic contact dermatitis: Possible alternative/in addition to irritant dermatitis if a sensitizing chemical (e.g., cleaner, fragrance) is involved. Itchy involvement and chronic exposure to cleaning agents make this plausible; patch testing could help confirm.
A: Atopic/hand eczema (hand dermatitis): Possible inflammatory eczema of the hands, which can present with dry, cracked, itchy hands. Considered given chronicity and location, though no personal history of atopy is noted.
T: Traumatic/irritant friction dermatitis: Mechanical irritation from repetitive cleaning tasks could contribute to fissuring and cracking, especially with irregular glove use.
E: Xerosis due to diabetes/metabolic factors: Diabetes can predispose to dry skin and fissuring; generalized dryness noted (more prominent on hands, with milder leg involvement). This could contribute to or worsen the presentation.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Strongly supported by occupational exposure to cleaning products, frequent hand washing and glove use inconsistency, palm-dominant involvement with fissures and itch, and chronic course over several months.
supporting_evidence: Palmar involvement with cracking and itching
Chronic onset (months) compatible with irritant contact dermatitis
opposing_evidence: No specific allergen or patch-test data yet

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Plausible given similar exposure to cleaning agents; allergic sensitization can occur with occupational chemicals; symptoms (pruritus, fissuring) fit dermatitis spectrum. Patch testing could identify specific allergens.
supporting_evidence: Exposure to cleaning chemicals without universal glove protection
opposing_evidence: No identified allergen or patch-test result yet
No acute widespread dermatitis or vesicular eruption described

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Hand dermatitis/eczema (including possible atopic dermatitis component)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Chronic dry, itchy hands with fissures are consistent with hand eczema/dermatitis; can be exacerbated by irritants or allergens in cleaners; presentation could reflect a general eczema phenotype affecting the hands.
supporting_evidence: Chronic hand involvement with dryness and itching
Response expected to steroids and moisturizers in many eczema variants
opposing_evidence: Lack of typical vesicular dyshidrosis or widespread eczematous plaques described

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Xerosis with fissuring related to diabetes/metabolic dryness
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Diabetes can predispose to dry skin and fissuring; generalized dryness is present (also on legs). However, the focal palmar cracking with itching points more toward contact dermatitis than simple xerosis alone.
supporting_evidence: Dryness noted on legs and hands
opposing_evidence: Palms show inflammatory changes (itch, fissuring) beyond simple xerosis
Local exposure to irritants is a more compelling driver in this presentation
